description.narrative:
The responses in Mozambique aims to address the needs of people affected by the cyclones in the region. Humanitarian efforts will provide support to people in need through a multi-sectoral approach, including e.g. access to clean drinking water, hygiene kits and GBV referrals. Much of the infrastructure has been damaged, and we will e.g. support water rehabilitation for schools and health clinics.
The Oxfam/KULIMA project will strengthen the capacity of essential WASH <(>&<)> protection services, to the affected population as informed by the multisectoral RNA of UNOCHA which was conducted in consultation w/ affected communities, INGD, UNICEF, WFP, UNHCR <(>&<)> INGOs. The project will be implemented in Monapo, Ilha de Moçambique <(>&<)> Mossuril districts of Nampula which were hit hardest. In alignment w/ WASH Cluster <(>&<)> SPHERE Std. we will provide WASH facilities to affected communities, incl. inclusivelatrines models, dignity <(>&<)> hygiene kits (composition = 3 soap, 5 toothbrushes w/ toothpaste, 1 lantern, 3 blankets, 3 mosquito nets, and water rations (strd of 20/25 ltrs a day). In total, we will reach 20,000 people (4000HH no double counting) with WASH activities <(>&<)> protection integrated. We will distribute 6750 hygiene kits; construct 350 latrines; rehabilitate sanitation infrastructure in 9 schools <(>&<)> 9 health facilities; rehabilitate 30 water pts; raise awareness on hygiene promotion, <(>&<)> sanitation through radio; <(>&<)> distribute menstrual hygiene kits to 1500 ppl. Consistent monitoring <(>&<)> evaluation will be conducted to ensure project effectiveness. Gender <(>&<)> Protection will be mainstreamed into all activities, following Oxfam’s Gender in Emergencies guidelines. A rapid gender analysis will inform project needs, ensuring that interventions are inclusive <(>&<)> sensitive to specific needs of women <(>&<)> girls. To enhance protection outcomes, we will hold information sessions to raise awareness on e.g. GBV. Community-based protection committees <(>&<)> at least 9 community-based protection networks will be set up to identify risks <(>&<)> respond to protection concerns. We'll work with gov. representatives at district level to facilitate referrals for GBV. Oxfam coordinated w/ DRA partners and specifically Plan (same target districts) to ensure complementarities <(>&<)> avoid duplication.KULIMA/Oxfam participates at national, provincial <(>&<)> district (KULIMA only) level cluster meetings on WASH <(>&<)> protection.
Oxfam in Mozambique is committed to localization via equitable partnerships w/ local actors: 53% of budget is for KULIMA <(>&<)> Oxfam’s humanitarian response strategy was codesigned <(>&<)> signed off by partners incl. KULIMA. The Action uses a hybrid implementation approach where activities under both sectors are shared btw Oxfam <(>&<)> KULIMA for efficiency, diversity <(>&<)> complementarity of experiences. KULIMA has a strong local presence via its Nampula office, incl. all targeted heavily affected districts. KULIMA led consultations w/ affected communities to inform project design <(>&<)> leads direct implementation of most activities: fix water pts, distribute WASH kits, GBV messaging, facilitate community mobilization <(>&<)> beneficiary selection etc. Oxfam builds latrines, distributes dignity kits <(>&<)> fixes water infrastructure while mainstreaming protection. Oxfam also integrates Gender, Safeguarding, Safe Programming, MEAL <(>&<)> Learning; provides technical support/security mgt to KULIMA; <(>&<)> monitors overall performance incl. on hum. standards. KULIMA is a member of the provincial and district Emergency Operational Councils (COEs); joined the COEs’ monitoring <(>&<)> needs assessment missions; and participates in coordination meetings. It’s a member of, among others, the WASH, Protection <(>&<)> FSL Clusters. Oxfam coordinated w/ all prospective JR members to align response plans, incl. separate correspondence w/ Plan due to same target locations. This’ll continue during project implementation w/ KULIMA participation.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
